corpus_row.citation: Horz W, Altenburger W (1981) Nucleotide sequence of mouse satellite DNA. Nucleic Acids Res 9(3):683-696. Claim supported: determination of the mouse satellite (major satellite) repeat unit sequence and its tandem, internally sub-repeated organisation.
corpus_row.expected_class: not a TE - pericentromeric major satellite tandem repeat (234 bp monomer); satellite DNA, not a mobile element
corpus_row.why_safe: Confusion axis: highly abundant tandem repeat that trips repeat-content and low-complexity masking, which is the same signal many pipelines use to nominate TE candidates - but it has no ORF, no RT, no transposase, no LTRs and no TIRs, so it is a pure repeat-content false positive rather than a domain false positive. Tool-independence: satellite identity was established by buoyant-density fractionation and direct sequencing of the isolated satellite fraction, an experimental definition with no annotation step. The record length (234 bp) is the major-satellite monomer itself, so the deposit is the repeat unit, not a clone containing it. Complements the excluded human alpha-satellite row (X07685) with a rodent satellite of independent origin.
